sources.title: Galin L. Jones, On the Markov Chain Central Limit Theorem
sources.locator: Complete 24-page arXiv PDF; §§2–4, especially Theorem 2, Theorems 5–9, and Corollary 1.
sources.reading_verification: The full PDF was opened and inspected. Read the total-variation rate definition, mixing coefficients, Theorem 2 and its rate-to-alpha argument, the full proof of Corollary 1, Theorems 5–8 and their exact moment/rate hypotheses, and Theorem 9. The source defers the proofs of the classical sequence CLTs; this batch records that gap rather than presenting the statements as locally proved.

contents.name: Stationary strong, uniform, and maximal-correlation coefficients
contents.support: Definitions are transcribed with the repository event-supremum convention; the local observation-factor lemma proves coefficient contraction.

contents.name: Total-variation rate controls strong mixing when the envelope is integrable
contents.support: The local proof bounds each future-event function by the total-variation dual estimate and integrates the envelope directly.

contents.name: Geometric ergodicity plus reversibility yields exponential rho mixing
contents.support: The exact conclusion is retained; its nontrivial spectral-gap proof remains an owner escalation.

contents.name: Strong-mixing CLT conditions
contents.support: The bounded, L2+delta, and exponential-log-moment hypotheses and their covariance conclusions are stated exactly; the classical CLT proofs are not supplied locally.

contents.name: Rho-mixing CLT condition
contents.support: The square-integrability and summable-rho condition are stated exactly; the theorem proof is escalated.

contents.name: Uniform-mixing CLT condition
contents.support: The square-root-phi summability hypothesis and uniform-ergodic specialization are stated exactly; the theorem proof is escalated.

contents.name: Six Markov-chain CLT sufficient regimes
contents.support: All six cases are retained, including both polynomial alternatives, the geometric logarithmic moment case, reversibility, and uniform ergodicity.

contents.name: Geometric ergodicity and integrability of a rate envelope
contents.support: Jones invokes the drift characterization and the Meyn–Tweedie invariant-moment theorem; the full local equivalence proof is not supplied and is escalated.

contents.name: Uniform ergodicity implies uniform mixing

sources.title: James M. Flegal and Galin L. Jones, Batch means and spectral variance estimators in Markov chain Monte Carlo
sources.locator: Complete 38-page arXiv PDF; OBM definition in §3, Theorem 2 and Corollary 1, and Appendix B.3.
sources.reading_verification: The complete PDF was opened and inspected. Read Assumptions 2–3, the OBM formula, Theorem 2, Corollary 1, the SIC definition and Lemma 3, and the complete Appendix B.3 proof. Appendix B.3 proceeds through a Brownian approximation and quadratic-form bounds; its SIC lemma cites Bednorz–Latuszyński and Jones et al. instead of proving that input. The source SIC definition requires positive finite asymptotic standard deviation, while Theorem 2 omits strict positivity; both facts are recorded as proof-route and boundary escalations.

contents.support: The exact source statement is retained. Its local proof is escalated because Appendix B.3 requires an imported strong invariance principle and Brownian/quadratic-form estimates.

sources.title: Olle Häggström and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, On Variance Conditions for Markov Chain CLTs
sources.locator: Complete 13-page author-hosted PDF; introductory variance-condition discussion and remarks on covariance summability.
sources.reading_verification: The complete short paper was opened and inspected. Read the discussion distinguishing absolute covariance summability, variance-limit identities, and existence of a Markov-chain CLT. This is used as a caution against treating covariance convergence as a CLT proof.

contents.name: Covariance summability does not replace a CLT argument
contents.support: The definition states that covariance summability alone neither proves a CLT nor identifies its weak-limit variance.

sources.title: Sean P. Meyn and Richard L. Tweedie, Markov Chains and Stochastic Stability, second edition
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 567-page PDF; Theorem 14.3.7, printed p. 349; Theorem 15.3.3, printed p. 377; Theorem 15.4.1 proof, printed pp. 379–381.
sources.reading_verification: The complete second-edition PDF was downloaded from the authors’ site. The browser text extraction for relevant pages was garbled, so the PDF was rendered with MuPDF and the complete displayed arguments were inspected. Theorem 14.3.7 proves an invariant drift-moment bound; Theorem 15.3.3 proves the f-geometric-regularity/drift equivalence; Theorem 15.4.1 converts the f-Kendall petite-set drift route to a geometric TV rate. This exposes the missing local f-Kendall petite/f-geometric-regularity interface; no proof is claimed for that gap.

searches.query: Meyn Tweedie Markov Chains and Stochastic Stability author PDF geometric ergodicity Theorem 14.3.7
searches.outcome: Located the authors’ full second-edition PDF and inspected the relevant theorem pages.

contents.name: Invariant measure integrates a drift function
contents.support: The proof integrates the drift inequality via the ergodic theorem; the converse geometric-to-drift construction remains a significant unresolved local prerequisite.

contents.name: Geometric regularity is characterized by a drift function
contents.support: The proof constructs the drift function from the renewal-potential kernel; the required f-Kendall petite definitions and full route are not local.

contents.name: Drift and petite-set route to geometric total-variation convergence
contents.support: The proof reduces through accessible atoms, strongly aperiodic cases, and skeleton chains. This confirms why the rate-envelope implication is escalated rather than imported as an unproved slogan.
